test_title: PYST 26: SSC CHSL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 09 Jul, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Consider AD is a tangent to a circle of radius 6 cm. AC is a secant meeting the circle at B and CD is a diameter. If AB is 7 cm, then the value of AC (in cm) is:
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 6 cm

AB = 7 cm

CD = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

**Formula used:**

AD² = AC × AB

AC² - CD² = AD²

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b186b8aac889f8998a954c1157c7da19637a4433557a57e81575aa4777b0ba34.png] 

Substituting the values in the Tangent-Secant Theorem:

AC² - 12² = AC × 7

⇒ AC² - 144 = 7AC

⇒ AC² - 7AC - 144 = 0

This is a quadratic equation, solving using the quadratic formula:

⇒ AC2 - 16AC + 9AC - 144 = 0

⇒ AC(AC - 16) + 9(AC - 16) = 0

⇒ (AC - 16)(AC + 9) = 0

⇒ AC = 16 or AC = -9

⇒ AC = 16 cm (since length cannot be negative)

**∴ The value of AC is 16 cm.**
